commit_message:
avformat/mlvdec: demux LJ92 huffman comressed frames

A minimal DNG header is added to each LJ92 compressed frame, allowing
thme to be decoded by the TIFF decoder. The TIFF decoder is responsible
for setting up the MJPEG decoder, signalling the correct s->bayer flag,
and setting pix_fmt.

The LJ92 compressed frames can be muxed out to DNG files, and manipulated
in DNG software. Tested with darktable and rawtherapee.

Contributor: South East <8billion.people@gmail.com>

findings.title: Unchecked attacker-controlled `size` leads to integer overflow and heap-buffer-overflow in get_packet_lj92()
findings.message: get_packet_lj92() takes a 64-bit `size` value that is derived, in read_packet(), from an unsigned 32-bit value read straight from the MLV file (block size minus a few fixed header fields and an attacker-controlled `space` field). Neither read_packet() nor get_packet_lj92() validates that `size` is within a sane range before it is used. Inside get_packet_lj92(), the packet buffer is allocated with `av_new_packet(pkt, size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE)`. Because `size` is attacker-controlled and unchecked, `size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE` can overflow (or otherwise not match the amount actually written), and the subsequent `avio_read(pbio, pkt->data + header_size, size)` can then write `size` bytes past the end of the allocated packet buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow. Additionally, in read_packet(), `size` is decremented by fixed amounts (12, optionally 8) and by the attacker-controlled `space` value (`size -= space;`) without first checking that `size` is large enough, allowing an unsigned underflow that produces a huge `size` value which is then passed straight into get_packet_lj92() or used for the audio packet size calculation.
findings.suggestion: Validate the `size` value before it is used to allocate/copy memory. In get_packet_lj92(), reject sizes that would overflow the allocation (e.g. `if ((uint64_t)size > INT32_MAX - MAX_HEADER_SIZE) return AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME;` before calling av_new_packet). In read_packet(), check that `size` is large enough before each subtraction (e.g. verify `size >= 8` before subtracting the crop/pan fields, and `size >= space + 4` before subtracting `space`) so that the unsigned `size` variable cannot underflow to a huge value that is later passed into get_packet_lj92() or used to compute the audio packet length.

ground_truth.root_cause: Missing/insufficient bounds validation on an attacker-controlled `size` (and the related `space` field) before it is used in unsigned arithmetic (subtraction that can underflow) and in a size-plus-constant allocation (addition that can overflow), both feeding directly into memory allocation and copy operations.
